candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture Team,

I’m writing to join AWA’s Talent Network because your work sits exactly where my experience and my heart meet: helping young people and their families through some of the hardest moments of their lives.

For more than 25 years, I have designed and facilitated learning programs, coached leaders and individuals, and coordinated group programs in person and online, in English and in Spanish. Early in my career in Venezuela, I co-facilitated a community prevention program for adolescents sponsored by Empresas Polar, with workshops on substance use and teen pregnancy prevention for teens living near the company’s facilities. That experience showed me how much prevention depends on reaching families in their own language and reality.

This work is also personal. Addiction to alcohol and drugs has touched my own family, and I have lost a young family member to its consequences. I now have four young grandchildren, and the idea of contributing to prevention efforts that protect children like them means a great deal to me.

I believe I could add value to AWA by supporting staff training and onboarding, developing educational workshops for families, especially Spanish-speaking families, or helping coordinate programs so that teens and parents stay engaged and informed. I’m based in Miami, fully bilingual, and comfortable working remotely or on-site in Miami.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to learn how I could support your team and the families you serve.

Warm regards,
Esther Leon
(713) 504-7640 · leoncesther@gmail.com · linkedin.com/in/esther-leon-ld

Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Operations position within your adolescent mental health PHP/IOP program. With approximately 12 years of experience working with individuals with autism, behavioral challenges, and social-emotional needs, I bring a strong foundation in behavioral support, staff training, leadership, and program structure. My professional background has allowed me to develop a thorough understanding of what it takes to create safe, consistent, and supportive environments for both clients and staff.

My experience began at Ramapo for Children, where I worked in several capacities, including lifeguard, swim instructor, and Toolbox Specialist. During my time there, I worked closely with neurodiverse individuals and those with behavioral and emotional challenges. As a Toolbox Specialist, I developed and implemented individualized behavioral strategies, problem-solved challenging situations, and trained other staff members on how to effectively respond to and manage difficult behaviors. This experience helped establish my leadership skills and taught me the importance of staff development, consistency, and individualized support.

Over the years, I have continued to build on that foundation through my work as a Registered Behavior Technician. I have approximately four years of experience implementing behavior intervention plans, collecting and analyzing behavioral data, collaborating with BCBAs, and maintaining strong relationships with clients and their families. I have worked with children and adolescents with varying levels of behavioral and communication needs, including individuals who require significant support with emotional regulation and challenging behaviors.

Beyond my direct clinical experience, I consider myself a natural leader who values accountability, teamwork, and clear communication. I have experience training and guiding staff, modeling appropriate interventions, and helping others develop the skills and confidence needed to work effectively with challenging populations. I understand that successful programs depend on more than clinical services alone. They require organized daily operations, effective communication, staff coordination, accurate documentation, strong safety practices, and the ability to adapt when unexpected challenges arise.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my behavioral health experience with my leadership abilities and passion for working with adolescents. While my background has primarily been in direct service, it has given me firsthand insight into the operational challenges staff face and the systems necessary to maintain a successful program. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my leadership in utilization review, payer relations, and revenue cycle management can support your team and the patients you serve. Thank you for your time and consideration, and I look forward to connecting with you.

Sincerely,

Sean P. Priest, LPN

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the Adolescent Wellness Academy team in Boca Raton. Your mission to provide adolescents with a safe, supportive environment where they feel seen, understood, and genuinely cared for deeply resonates with both my personal values and professional purpose.

As a board-certified Health and Wellness Coach, Hypnotherapist, and Fitness Instructor, I bring a holistic approach to physical, mental, and emotional well-being. My work focuses on helping individuals develop healthier habits, manage stress, build self-awareness, strengthen emotional resilience, and create positive, sustainable changes in their lives.

I strongly believe that the foundations of overall wellness should be taught from an early age. Equipping adolescents with practical tools for emotional regulation, stress management, mindfulness, healthy habits, and self-awareness can better prepare them to navigate the challenges of life and an increasingly demanding world. These are invaluable life skills that can positively influence their well-being well into adulthood.

As a mother, I also appreciate the unique pressures adolescents face today and the importance of having compassionate, trustworthy individuals who can support and guide them through this formative stage of life.

I believe my background in health and mindset coaching, behavior change, mindfulness, breathwork, and nervous system regulation would complement AWA’s multidisciplinary approach. November 25, 2026

Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy Boca Raton, FL

Re: Creative Group Facilitator – Adolescent Mental Health

Dear AWA Hiring Team,

I'm excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator role. I'm a K–8 art teacher with a B.A. in Studio Art and Psychology from Florida State University, and I'm currently earning my M.S. in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Walden University. I've spent my career at the point where art, behavior and emotional growth meet. Helping teens build confidence and coping skills through creative work is exactly the kind of work I want to be doing.

Leading groups with adolescents. 
I teach art to students in kindergarten through 8th grade, including middle schoolers on the edge of the age group AWA serves. Every day I plan and lead hands-on lessons that work for students with very different skill levels, attention spans and comfort with being creative in front of peers. I created a tiered behavior escalation framework for my classroom, so I can handle tough group moments calmly and consistently while keeping the room safe for everyone. After my first year, I built a full curriculum by hand, planned month by month so lessons build on each other and stay fresh.

Adapting creative work to each person. 
As a Clinical Educator at Cayer Behavioral Group, an ABA practice, I worked with K–5 children with autism. I used each child's data to design sensory-friendly, hands-on activities tailored to their needs. I worked alongside the clinical team and advocated for the kids, especially around their feelings. Earlier, as a nanny, I ran "Creative Play" sessions with short art lessons built into each child's care plan. I've learned that the activity is only the vehicle. What matters is whether each participant feels safe enough to try.

A clinical lens. 
My psychology coursework at FSU included abnormal psychology, neurodivergence and neuroscience. At Walden, I'm studying counseling techniques and trauma-informed care. In a PHP or IOP setting, that helps me understand what teens may be carrying into the room. It also helps me know when to invite expression and when to give space, and how to document what I see in a way that's useful to the clinical team. I'm used to timely documentation from tracking student progress data and keeping records in my school's gradebook system.

My own creative background goes beyond the classroom.
It includes studio art, commissioned signage work and clarinet performance, so I can offer a range of expressive activities, from drawing and collage to music and mindful making. I'd love to bring that range, along with real care for teens, to your village.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I could support AWA's creative programming.

Sincerely,

Justine Therrien

candidates.cover_letter:
10/27/2026
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy,
I am writing to express my interest in the Adolescent Mental Health Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern with an MSW from Florida Atlantic University, I am dedicated to working alongside vulnerable children and families, and I would welcome the chance to bring my hands-on clinical experience and my commitment to growth to your team.
In my current role as Family Advocate / Clinical Case Manager at CityHouse, I deliver crisis intervention, de-escalation, and stabilization services, conduct comprehensive psychosocial and needs assessments with resident families, and provide counseling to children and families using evidence-based, trauma-informed interventions. I develop individualized treatment plans with measurable goals in collaboration with clients and the clinical team, then monitor progress and adjust plans as needs change. I also assisted in developing a children's therapeutic service program and an intentional therapeutic room across two campuses, a space designed so children feel safe and supported.
My MSW internship at CityHouse deepened my work with children and their caregivers. I created and facilitated an 8-week social-emotional learning group for children ages 8-12, and I advocated for IEP and educational needs for elementary-aged children, supporting mothers at parent-teacher conferences. Earlier, as a BSW intern and Behavioral Technician at Aces for Autism, I provided 1:1 applied behavior analysis sessions for children, including children with autism spectrum disorder, and completed clinical documentation. Together, these experiences taught me to meet each family where they are and build on their strengths.
What draws me to social work is the opportunity to walk alongside children and families through difficult moments and help them recognize their own strengths. I am currently accruing clinical hours toward LCSW licensure in Florida, and I am committed to ongoing growth through supervision, training, and hands-on practice.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy, and I can be reached at 845-600-5746 or accurson02@yahoo.com.
Sincerely,
Nadia Accurso, MSW Registered Clinical Social Work Intern

Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Therapy position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern (RCSWI), I am passionate about supporting individuals through life’s challenges and helping them develop the tools and skills necessary to achieve emotional wellness, resilience, and personal growth. I believe my clinical experience, diverse background working with various populations, and dedication to providing compassionate, client-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role, I provide therapeutic services to youth, adolescents, and adults with a wide range of mental health and behavioral health needs, including PTSD, depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, and substance use disorders. I utilize evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and trauma-informed care, to help clients navigate challenges, strengthen coping skills, regulate emotions, and work toward their individualized treatment goals. I strive to create a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment where clients feel heard, respected, and empowered throughout their healing journey.

In addition to my clinical experience, I have worked with diverse and vulnerable populations, including individuals impacted by domestic violence, substance use, homelessness, disabilities, and challenges associated with aging. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach each individual with empathy, patience, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the unique circumstances that influence mental health and overall well-being. I recognize the importance of meeting clients where they are, building trusting therapeutic relationships, and tailoring interventions to their individual needs and strengths.

I am a driven, hardworking, compassionate, and dedicated professional who values collaboration, continued learning, and professional growth. I am committed to helping clients recognize their strengths, overcome barriers, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my skills and passion to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support the emotional and psychological well-being of the individuals and families served by your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, therapeutic approach, and commitment to quality mental health care align with the needs of your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With over 15 years of experience as a Medical Claims Analyst and remote work experience since 2020, I am eager to bring my healthcare knowledge and passion for helping others into the behavioral health field.

Throughout my career, I have developed strong skills in insurance verification, claims analysis, healthcare documentation, and problem resolution. I am familiar with electronic medical record systems and understand the importance of confidentiality, accuracy, and effective communication. My experience also includes training new employees and guiding colleagues through complex healthcare processes.

My passion for mental health and substance use treatment is deeply personal. Having a father who struggled with addiction allowed me to witness the importance of addressing mental health alongside substance use. His experience inspired my desire to advocate for accessible treatment, early intervention, and compassionate care without judgment.

Although my professional experience has been primarily in medical claims, I am eager to expand my knowledge and apply my transferable skills within behavioral health admissions. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be one of the most vulnerable moments in an individual's or family's life. I would welcome the opportunity to be a compassionate first point of contact, providing clarity, encouragement, and support throughout the admissions process.

I am drawn to this opportunity because it aligns with both my professional strengths and my personal values. I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to your team while continuing to grow within behavioral healthcare.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, dedication, and passion for helping others can contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,

Natasha Johnson

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. I bring a strong background in mental health services enrollment, client support, and high-volume customer engagement, along with a genuine passion for helping people access the support they need.

My connection to this work is both professional and personal. Growing up, I experienced periods of limited support around mental health, particularly during childhood and my early teenage years. Those experiences shaped my understanding of how difficult it can be to ask for help and how important it is to feel heard, respected, and supported when taking that first step. I have worked through those challenges, and today they give me an even stronger sense of purpose in the work I do. I want every person I interact with to feel that they are being met with patience, compassion, and genuine intent.

Professionally, I have experience helping individuals navigate sensitive situations, understand available services, discuss coverage and financial concerns, and take the next steps toward receiving support. At Lido Labs, I worked in mental health services enrollment, conducting a high volume of inbound and outbound interactions, assessing individual needs, explaining service options, and helping people move forward with solutions. I consistently exceeded performance goals while maintaining quality and a person-centered approach. My additional experience in education enrollment and Medicaid health plan support has strengthened my ability to guide people through complex processes, communicate clearly, and follow through on important details.

One of my greatest strengths is building trust. People tend to feel comfortable opening up to me, and I take that responsibility seriously. I understand that someone reaching out for mental health or substance use support may be experiencing uncertainty, fear, or vulnerability. I would approach every conversation with empathy while maintaining professionalism, respecting confidentiality, and helping individuals navigate the admissions process with clarity.

I would be proud to bring my experience, perspective, and commitment to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to making the admissions experience more supportive and accessible for the individuals and families you serve.

Sincerely,
Joshua Curtis

Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and professional experience in behavioral health, substance-use treatment, client support, and wellness services, I bring a strong foundation in compassionate communication and helping individuals navigate challenging periods in their lives.
During my time at Alternative to Meds Center, I worked within a behavioral health and substance-use treatment environment, where I supported individuals entering the program and helped orient newly admitted clients to program expectations, schedules, procedures, and available resources. I also facilitated groups and utilized electronic medical records for client documentation. This experience gave me an appreciation for how important the initial treatment experience can be in helping individuals feel supported, informed, and comfortable engaging in care.
In my current work as a Vocational Job Coach, I support individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities and co-occurring behavioral health challenges. My responsibilities include helping clients navigate new jobs, coordinate services, overcome practical barriers, and develop greater independence through individualized support. These experiences have strengthened my ability to communicate with people from diverse backgrounds, remain organized, and provide consistent follow-through.
My background also includes emergency medical services, holistic wellness coaching, and trauma-conscious practices. Across these settings, I have developed a patient-centered approach grounded in empathy, active listening, respect, and an understanding that seeking help can be an overwhelming experience for individuals and their families.
I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because of the important role admissions coordinators play in connecting people with appropriate care. Whether speaking with a concerned parent seeking support for their adolescent or an adult exploring recovery options, I understand the importance of meeting people with compassion while providing clear information and dependable guidance. Having grown up in South Florida near Davie, I also have a personal connection to the community your organizations serve and would welcome the opportunity to contribute to its well-being.
I would welcome the opportunity to bring my psychology background, behavioral health experience, EMR familiarity, and commitment to meaningful client support to your team.
Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss my qualifications.
Sincerely,
Ashtani Agni

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

Service isn't just something I do; it's part of who I am. Throughout my life, I've learned that success isn't only about having a job or earning a title. It's about the difference you make, the people you help, and how you overcome challenges. From serving in the Florida Army National Guard to working as a Public Safety Officer at Nemours Children's Hospital, my experiences have shaped me into the hardworking, dependable, and motivated person I am today.

I am excited to apply for a position with your organization because I believe my background, work ethic, and willingness to learn would make me a valuable addition to your team. I take pride in challenging myself, developing new skills, and giving my best effort in everything I do.

Serving in the Army National Guard has been one of my proudest accomplishments. The military has taught me discipline, teamwork, accountability, and leadership. It has also helped me remain calm under pressure and adapt when situations don't go as planned. One of the biggest lessons I've learned is that leadership isn't always about being in charge. Sometimes, it's about stepping up when others need help and taking responsibility when things become difficult. These are values I carry into my everyday life.

Currently, I work as a Public Safety Officer at Nemours Children's Hospital, where I help maintain a safe and welcoming environment for patients, families, visitors, and employees. Working in a children's hospital has shown me how important compassion, patience, and communication are. Many families experience stressful situations, and sometimes simply listening, offering reassurance, or showing kindness can make a difference. This position has taught me that professionalism isn't just about completing responsibilities but also about how you treat others.

My previous experience in hospitality and customer service has also helped me develop strong communication, problem-solving, and teamwork skills. Working in fast-paced environments taught me how to manage multiple responsibilities, stay organized, and maintain a positive attitude. I believe every position I've held has contributed to my personal and professional growth.

Outside of work, I am continuing my college education while balancing military responsibilities and being a father. Managing these commitments isn't always easy, but they motivate me to work harder and create a better future for my family. I want to build a meaningful career while setting a positive example for my children.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology, ongoing graduate studies in Social Work, and professional experience in behavioral health intake, case management, and substance use support, I bring a combination of clinical understanding, administrative coordination, and compassionate communication. As a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking professional, I am especially passionate about helping individuals and families overcome barriers to accessing mental health and substance use treatment.

In my current role as a Case Manager at EMC Behavioral, I work in a fully virtual environment, supporting children and adolescents experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. My responsibilities include conducting intake assessments, identifying service needs, verifying insurance, coordinating referrals, scheduling appointments, and maintaining accurate client documentation. Working remotely has strengthened my ability to independently manage my responsibilities, communicate effectively with clients and caregivers through virtual platforms, and ensure timely follow-up without requiring daily in-person supervision. I understand the importance of maintaining confidentiality, accurate documentation, and consistent communication when coordinating behavioral health services remotely.

Additionally, as a Bilingual Parent Support Specialist at Catholic Charities' Guadalupe Home, I support young mothers experiencing various challenges, including substance use concerns, in a residential shelter environment. My work involves providing trauma-informed support, assisting with behavioral and emotional challenges, communicating with residents, and maintaining accurate documentation. Working with individuals during vulnerable periods has taught me the importance of approaching difficult conversations with empathy, patience, and professionalism while helping individuals feel respected and supported.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because both programs serve populations with whom I have direct professional experience. I understand that individuals and families seeking behavioral health or substance use treatment may feel overwhelmed, uncertain, or afraid. I believe that providing clear information, listening without judgment, and following through on next steps can make a meaningful difference in their willingness and ability to access care. My experience with insurance verification, intake coordination, appointment scheduling, and client communication, combined with my ability to work independently in a fully remote environment, aligns closely with the responsibilities of this position.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my behavioral health experience, organizational skills, and bilingual communication abilities to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background can support your programs and the individuals and families you serve.

Sincerely,
Jennyfer Alvidrez

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in a position within your recovery or behavioral health organization. With experience as a Peer Recovery Specialist at Life Connection, along with my background in healthcare and patient support, I am passionate about helping individuals find hope, strength, and the resources they need to move forward in their recovery journey.

During my time at Life Connection, I provided one-on-one peer support, facilitated recovery support groups, assisted individuals with paperwork, and connected guests with community resources and services. I learned the importance of active listening, empathy, patience, confidentiality, and creating a safe and welcoming environment where individuals feel respected and understood.

My experience as a Certified Nursing Assistant and Certified Medication Aide has also strengthened my ability to care for others with compassion, dignity, and professionalism. I understand the importance of meeting people where they are, recognizing their individual needs, and providing support without judgment.

I believe recovery is about more than overcoming challenges. It is about helping people recognize their strengths, build confidence, and discover that a better future is possible. I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and passion for recovery to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and commitment to helping others can contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Shakra Simpson

candidates.summary:
I am a recent medical graduate with a strong commitment to research, community service, and leadership in healthcare. My interest in research began early during my three-year involvement in the INTEL Research Program (2015), where I participated in multiple projects and had the opportunity to present my work, “The Effects of Various Treatment Modalities on the Cortical-Striatal-Cerebellar Loop,” at the Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS). This formative experience sparked a lasting interest in scientific inquiry and continues to shape my academic and clinical pursuits.

During my undergraduate studies at the University of Central Florida, I further developed my research experience through a project titled “Comparative Analysis of Surgical Intervention vs. Physical Therapy in ACL Injury Recovery.” In addition to research, I was an active member of Phi Delta Epsilon medical fraternity, graduated from the UCF LEAD Scholars Honors Program, and consistently earned Dean’s List recognition for academic excellence.

In medical school, I have expanded my research involvement through collaboration with faculty at my institution, focusing on the role of artificial intelligence in COVID-19 contact tracing and its broader applications in healthcare. This work has contributed to two additional publications and strengthened my interest in the intersection of technology and medicine.

Alongside my academic and research pursuits, I remain actively engaged in student organizations that reflect my commitment to service and advocacy. I am particularly interested in contributing to community outreach efforts and advancing equity in medicine.

Overall, I am dedicated to developing into a compassionate, well-rounded physician who combines strong clinical skills with a commitment to research, service, and meaningful impact in healthcare.

candidates.cover_letter:
Good morning/afternoon, thank you for taking the time to read this. 

I have worked a couple different jobs over the last couple of years. My first job was at Panda Express right after I graduated high school. I was freshly moved out and starting college with a double major in english and physiology. I learned a lot at this job, even though I was there a short time. It taught me how to work with others in a fast paced environment, how to talk with upset customers and come to a fix with them. I also learned how to keep food fresh for as long as possible, how to get the most stubborn stains and smells out of my uniforms, and what cleaners worked best for every surface. 

While still going to school full time I decided to get something closer to me and applied at Starbucks. This job was interesting and by far the most fun. I spent a lot of time at Starbucks talking and listening to my customers. I learned their names, favorite drinks, and little pieces of their life’s. My favorite part of my shift would be the rush. It’s fast paced and everyone is in a “zone”, we all had our own stations to run but still had to move together to ensure a smooth rush. There was four baristas total making drinks and we all had our own place in the line. While working together we had to coordinate timing our orders with the person making food and taking the orders/handing them out.

After working at Starbucks for about a year, I got an opportunity to work at an ambulance company as a 911 call taker/dispatcher. I’ve grown up in the EMS environment, so it was always something I wanted to go into. At this job, I learned what that saying about if you work at a job, you love you never work a day in your life meant. At this point I had dropped out of college to pursue this career because I knew it’s what I wanted to do in the long run. we worked 12 hour shifts where we were cross trained in dispatching and call taking, normally I would be first up for phones. I answered 911 calls for all different number of things I took medical calls and psychiatric calls. During those calls, I would gather as much information as possible, such as scene safety, what the patient was wearing, and the reason behind why they called. The county that I worked in had a heavy population for drugs and homelessness. Most of my calls were for patients undergoing issues after a bad drug reaction or for psychiatric issues. Depending on how busy the day went, I would have to dispatch while being on the phone with a patient handling both radios and giving medical assistance to my caller. This job was hard, but it was also the best job I’ve ever had. I loved all the bright moments that brought me with my coworkers and my partners. It showed a lot of dark in the community that I lived in, but it also showed a lot of light.

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Team,

When someone reaches out for behavioral health or substance use treatment, that first phone call often happens on one of the hardest days of their life. As a Behavioral Health and Alcohol/Other Drug (BH/AOD) Case Manager and Emergency Communications Officer, I have spent my career being that steady, compassionate first voice—guiding individuals and families in crisis from an overwhelming moment toward clear, actionable care. I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) and Principles Recovery Center (PRC).

My background directly aligns with the clinical empathy, operational precision, and self-directed follow-through required to manage an admissions pipeline remotely:

- Behavioral Health & Substance Use Intake: During my three years as a BH/AOD Case Manager at Firelands Counseling and Recovery, I conducted holistic intake assessments, identified barriers to recovery, and guided clients through program eligibility, documentation gathering, and resource coordination. I know how to explain complex treatment options in plain, supportive language that helps clients and families feel heard and empowered.

- High-Volume Phone Triage & De-escalation: In my current role as a Communications Officer with the Erie County Sheriff’s Office, I manage high-volume inbound calls from individuals under acute stress. I use calm, active listening and structured interview techniques to gather vital demographic and safety information quickly while maintaining a warm, reassuring presence.

- EMR Accuracy, Eligibility Verification & Pipeline Management: Between my clinical documentation in Epic EMR, auditing legal records with zero error tolerance, and completing an M.S. in Data Analytics, I bring exceptional rigor to lead tracking, insurance and eligibility verification, and HIPAA-compliant recordkeeping. I thrive in autonomous environments where consistent follow-up ensures no caller falls through the cracks.

I deeply admire AWA and PRC’s family-centered, evidence-based approach to PHP and IOP care—supporting both teens and adults through co-occurring mental health and substance use challenges. My combination of a B.A. in Psychology, frontline behavioral health intake experience, and high-stakes communication skills makes me uniquely prepared to help your callers take their first step toward healing.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how I can support your admissions team and the families you serve.

Sincerely,

Kathryn Smith

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a background spanning healthcare support, remote patient advocacy, court administration, public service, and confidential records management, I bring a combination of interpersonal communication, organizational skills, and attention to detail that aligns well with the responsibilities of this position.

In my current role as a remote Patient Advocate with Kible Health d/b/a Understood Care, I assist individuals by listening to their concerns, communicating information, documenting interactions, and coordinating appropriate follow-up. This experience has strengthened my ability to approach sensitive conversations with patience, professionalism, and compassion while maintaining confidentiality.

My previous healthcare experience with Health Actions and Meadows of Monroeville also provided exposure to patient care environments, medical documentation, patient histories, and communication with patients and families. Additionally, my experience as a Court Specialist I with the State of Alabama required accuracy, discretion, procedural compliance, and effective communication with individuals navigating sometimes difficult and unfamiliar circumstances.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because of its emphasis on helping individuals and families navigate the process of accessing appropriate treatment. I understand that the initial interaction with an admissions coordinator can be especially important for someone seeking help. I would approach that responsibility with empathy, professionalism, and a commitment to making the process as clear and supportive as possible.

Although my professional background has focused on patient advocacy, healthcare support, and administrative coordination rather than direct behavioral health admissions, I bring a strong foundation in patient-facing communication, documentation, confidentiality, and independent remote work. I am confident in my ability to learn specialized admissions procedures, insurance verification workflows, and the systems necessary to support your programs effectively.

I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and transferable skills could contribute to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely 
Alexis A. Dailey

Education

* Patient-centered communication and active listening.

Dear Hiring Team,

I'm applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. When someone calls a treatment program, they are often scared and unsure of what to do next. I want to be the person who answers with warmth and gets them to a clear next step.

I currently work in two roles. At Engaging Thoughts Counseling, I support the VP of Compliance and work with the Clinical Director and clinical staff on HIPAA documentation, confidential records, and compliance reporting. This is my daily work in a behavioral health setting. It has taught me to handle sensitive information carefully and to manage my own calendar and deadlines without daily direction. At the American Red Cross, I coordinate intake appointments, answer incoming calls, register clients, and follow up. I also keep confidential client profiles and send weekly reports to regional leadership.

My background fits the core of this role:
- **Calls and follow-up:** At Family Care Management, I managed client registration, intake documentation, scheduling, and multi-line phone inquiries for more than three years. At Universal Orlando, I helped 150+ people a day with sensitive requests and used Salesforce CRM to verify accounts and track every follow-up.
- **Bilingual and trained in psychology:** I'm fluent in English and Spanish, and I hold a B.A. in Psychology. I can explain next steps plainly to a teen's parent or an adult in crisis, in the language they're most comfortable in.
- **Documentation and compliance:** I know HIPAA expectations well, and I'm careful about tracking every lead and conversation accurately.

I haven't yet worked in a treatment center's admissions department, and I won't pretend otherwise. I do bring the skills this role depends on: calm phone presence, consistent follow-up, accurate records, and respect for confidentiality. I learn systems quickly. I did it with Salesforce, and I would approach Kipu and insurance verification the same way. I'm available Monday through Friday, full-time, and ready to work independently from home.

Thank you for your time. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can support your admissions team and the families who call you.

Sincerely,
Anthony Martinez

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology, experience in behavioral health and crisis stabilization, and current enrollment in Virginia Commonwealth University's Master of Education in Counselor Education program, I bring a strong foundation in compassionate client care, service coordination, and mental health advocacy.

In my current role as a Foster Care Case Manager, I serve as a point of contact for children, families, treatment providers, and community partners. My responsibilities include coordinating services, facilitating communication across multidisciplinary teams, maintaining confidential documentation, and ensuring families receive appropriate resources and support. This experience has strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, work independently, and provide consistent follow-through while navigating sensitive and complex circumstances.

Additionally, my experience as a Qualified Mental Health Professional in residential crisis stabilization, therapeutic day treatment, and community-based behavioral health has equipped me to support individuals experiencing emotional distress and complex mental health challenges. I understand the importance of approaching each interaction with empathy, patience, professionalism, and cultural responsiveness. I am also comfortable navigating electronic documentation systems, handling confidential information, and collaborating with providers to support continuity of care.

What particularly draws me to this opportunity is the ability to serve as an initial point of connection for individuals and families seeking treatment. Reaching out for mental health or substance use services can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience. I am passionate about creating an environment in which individuals feel heard, respected, and supported while receiving clear guidance regarding their next steps.

I am confident that my behavioral health experience, organizational skills, ability to build rapport, and commitment to client-centered care would allow me to contribute meaningfully to your admissions team. I would welcome the opportunity to support both programs in reducing barriers to treatment and connecting individuals and families with the care they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and professional values align with your organization's mission.

Sincerely,

Rorie Spencer

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and passion for behavioral health align with the needs of your organization. Sincerely,
Jordan Wright

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Throughout my professional career in healthcare journalism, hospitality, customer service, and communications, I have developed a genuine passion for helping others. I understand that individuals and families seeking mental health or substance use treatment may be experiencing some of the most difficult moments of their lives. Being met with compassion, patience, and understanding can make a meaningful difference in their journey toward healing.

My background in healthcare journalism has provided me with opportunities to interview medical professionals, research health-related topics, and communicate sensitive information with accuracy, discretion, and empathy. These experiences have strengthened my ability to listen attentively, ask appropriate questions, and communicate complex information clearly.

With more than 25 years of hospitality experience, I am comfortable handling inquiries, resolving concerns, coordinating schedules, and managing multiple responsibilities in fast-paced environments. My freelance journalism and marketing experience has also strengthened my ability to work remotely, manage deadlines independently, and maintain consistent communication and follow-through.

While my professional background has not been directly in behavioral health admissions, I bring transferable skills, a compassionate approach, and a genuine willingness to learn your admissions procedures, insurance verification processes, and CRM and EMR systems.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to an organization dedicated to improving the lives of adolescents, adults, and their families. I believe that every individual deserves to be heard, respected, and supported, particularly during challenging circumstances.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, dedication, and interpersonal skills could benefit your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Melissa Billie Clark

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment. As a psychology student at Salisbury University with hands on experience in behavioral health, healthcare, and administrative support, I believe I have a strong foundation that would allow me to contribute positively to your team.

In my current role as a Registered Behavior Technician, I work one on one with children with autism who have varying levels of support needs. My responsibilities include supporting communication and social skill development, implementing individualized teaching strategies, documenting behavioral data and progress, and communicating with parents, caregivers, and clinical supervisors. I am also actively working toward obtaining my RBT certification to continue developing my knowledge and experience in behavioral health. This position has strengthened my patience, empathy, and understanding of the importance of individualized care.

Previously, I worked as a Phlebotomist with BioLife Plasma Services, where I gained valuable healthcare experience. I was responsible for maintaining accurate medical records, checking patients in, scheduling and managing appointments, answering questions, and helping individuals feel comfortable throughout their visits. My previous administrative experience also helped me develop strong organizational, communication, and documentation skills.

As someone pursuing a degree in psychology, I am passionate about mental health and helping individuals receive the care and support they need. I understand that seeking treatment can be an overwhelming experience for both adolescents and their families, and I would approach every interaction with compassion, patience, and professionalism. I would love the opportunity to use my background in psychology, behavioral health, and healthcare to help families navigate the admissions process and connect with appropriate treatment services.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and passion for helping others could make me a valuable addition to your team. I look forward to hearing from you.

Dear Hiring Team,

I'm applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role because it fits well with not only the previous experience I have but where I want to be. I would genuinely love to take the first phone call, answer the insurance questions, and conduct the follow-through that gets someone from "I'm thinking about it" to a scheduled intake for treatment.

At Helio Health, a substance use treatment provider in Syracuse, I guided new patients through admission. I welcomed people on what was often an emotionally complex and sensitive day. I provided assistance with completing their intake paperwork, performed safety searches, answered questions and coordinated with staff to ensure each patient's needs were met while documenting in Avatar EHR. I also coordinated with clinical staff to make sure each person's needs were handed off clearly. I also completed my CASAC 350-hour education at Helio Health's training institute, so I understand the treatment side, not just the scheduling side.

Before that, I spent four years at Excellus BlueCross BlueShield explaining behavioral health and substance use disorder benefits, including intensive outpatient programs, to members and providers. Later, at Kopp Billing, I verified eligibility and benefits across UHC, Fidelis, Empire, and Medicaid and worked out what patients would actually owe. That means I can tell a worried parent or adult caller what their coverage likely looks like in plain language, and I know when a question needs to go to someone else.

In my current role, I work remotely, handling 45 to 60 calls a day in Salesforce with people facing utility shutoffs. Many callers are stressed or embarrassed, and my job is to calm things down, lay out their options, and follow through. I've earned 100% CSAT every month after my first, cut my transfer rate from 15% to 7% in about a week, and escalated one call to a supervisor since December 2025. I document every call in real time and manage my own follow-ups without someone checking in on me.

Families calling your admissions line need someone warm, clear, and persistent. That's how I work. I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I can help Principles Recovery and Adolescent Wellness Academy connect more callers to care.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Gabrielle Licastri

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With over four years of experience in case management, client engagement, behavioral health support, and resource coordination, I bring a compassionate, organized, and client-focused approach to helping individuals navigate challenging circumstances and connect with the services they need.

Throughout my career, I have worked directly with individuals experiencing housing instability, mental health challenges, and other complex barriers to stability and well-being. In my current role as a Client Engagement Specialist with The Road Home, I serve as an initial point of contact for individuals entering shelter, gathering important information, completing intake paperwork, and helping clients navigate the next steps in their housing journey. I understand the importance of creating a welcoming, supportive first impression, particularly when someone is reaching out during a difficult period in their life.

My previous experience as a Case Manager and Employment Specialist with Asian Association of Utah strengthened my ability to manage a high-volume caseload of more than 55 clients while assessing individual needs, developing personalized care plans, and coordinating essential services. I regularly advocated for clients by connecting them with Medicaid, SNAP, housing resources, and Social Security services. My background also includes facilitating communication with interpreters, coordinating care among multiple providers, and maintaining thorough documentation to support continuity of services.

In addition to my behavioral health and case management experience, I bring a strong foundation in insurance verification and patient counseling from my time with Westwood Physical Therapy. I verified benefits with more than 30 insurance companies, explained coverage and anticipated costs to patients, and coordinated additional visits by submitting medical necessity documentation. This experience would be valuable when helping prospective clients and families understand insurance coverage and navigate the admissions process.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because I genuinely enjoy helping people find the assistance they need. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be overwhelming, and I believe every interaction should be approached with patience, empathy, clear communication, and respect. My training in Mental Health First Aid, de-escalation, CPR, and trauma-informed care has prepared me to communicate thoughtfully with individuals experiencing distress while helping them identify appropriate next steps.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my communication skills, leadership abilities, research skills, and experience coordinating client services to your admissions team. I am enthusiastic about the possibility of helping individuals and families take an important first step toward healing and accessing the care they deserve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and commitment to client-centered support could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,

Jennifer Winfree

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I recently applied for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position and wanted to share why this work
matters to me. When a parent calls about mental health or substance use treatment for their teen, they
may be worried and unsure where to start. I’d like to be the person who listens, explains the next step
clearly, and follows through on what I said I would do.

At True North Pediatrics, I helped families with patient intake, scheduling, referrals, and insurance
verification. I kept patient records up to date and followed up when information was missing. As a
Child Protective Investigator with the Florida Department of Children and Families, I spoke with
children and caregivers during difficult circumstances and documented sensitive information with
care. Both roles taught me how much it matters to stay calm, ask clear questions, and make sure
families know what happens next.
I’m fluent in English and Spanish, and I’ve supported clients by phone, email, and video. My studies in
forensic psychology and my training as a Christian Mental Health Coach have deepened my interest in
how families navigate the decision to seek help.

I’d bring that perspective to your admissions team along with the practical habits I’ve built in pediatric care: keeping track of referrals, protecting confidential information, and following up when a family is waiting for an answer.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to talk with you about how I can support your admissions team and the families who reach out to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Lizmar Encarnacion-Rosario

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, ongoing graduate studies in Forensic Psychology, and professional experience in behavioral health and human services, I have developed a strong understanding of the importance of compassionate communication, confidentiality, and connecting individuals and families with the appropriate support.

My previous experience as a Behavioral Technician and Case Manager Assistant allowed me to work closely with individuals with varying behavioral, developmental, and support needs. These roles strengthened my ability to communicate with families, navigate sensitive situations, maintain accurate documentation, and coordinate services while approaching each interaction with patience and professionalism. I also have experience working independently in remote investigative environments, where organization, attention to detail, managing multiple priorities, and consistent follow-through were essential.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to be part of someone’s first step toward receiving care. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be overwhelming, especially for adolescents and their families. I would bring a calm, empathetic, and reassuring approach to every interaction while ensuring callers receive clear information and guidance throughout the admissions process.

I am confident that my educational background, behavioral health experience, investigative skills, and ability to work independently would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your admissions team. I would welcome the opportunity to support both Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center in connecting individuals and families with the care they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience align with this position.

Sincerely,
Mikaela Albrecht

Dear Hiring Team,

I’m excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I bring direct intake experience in behavioral health and substance use treatment from my work at Oriana House and The Bluffs. I know how much it matters for someone who is reaching out for help to hear a calm, caring voice and end the conversation knowing what to do next.

As a Preschool Director and Director of Children and Family Ministries at Church at Six Forks, I guided families through enrollment, answered sensitive questions, maintained records in Procare, and followed up on paperwork. That work taught me to listen carefully, explain unfamiliar processes in plain language, and keep track of the details so families knew what to expect. I would bring that same care and follow-through to intake calls, assessment scheduling, and communication with families and referral partners.

I’m drawn to this role because it combines the part of intake I value most, helping people feel comfortable asking for help, with the practical work of getting them connected to care. I would welcome the opportunity to support teens, adults, and families as they take that first step.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d love the opportunity to talk with you about how my intake experience and work with families could support both programs.

Warmly,
Brianne Weishaar

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration and professional experience in admissions, administrative coordination, and customer service, I believe my background aligns well with the responsibilities of this role.

In my role as an Administrative Coordinator at the International Language Academy of Washington DC, I serve as the first point of contact for prospective students, guiding them through the admissions process, explaining program requirements, reviewing documentation, coordinating appointments, and maintaining accurate records. I also manage a high volume of phone calls and emails while working with individuals from diverse cultural backgrounds.

Previously, as General Manager at Executive Tysons Office Suites, I developed strong organizational, problem-solving, and communication skills while managing daily operations, client relationships, contracts, and administrative responsibilities.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to use my professional experience to make a meaningful difference in the lives of adolescents and their families. I understand the importance of approaching sensitive situations with empathy, patience, professionalism, and respect.

My experience in admissions has strengthened my ability to guide individuals through complex processes, address their concerns, and provide clear and compassionate support. I am confident that these skills would allow me to contribute effectively to your admissions team. Being bilingual in English and Spanish also allows me to communicate with and support families from diverse cultural backgrounds.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, skills, and commitment to helping others could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,

Andrea Aparicio

As a Licensed Practical Nurse with experience in clinical care coordination, case management, insurance verification, patient intake, and emergency response, I bring a strong foundation in patient advocacy and healthcare navigation.

In my current role with SC House Calls, I coordinate patient care, manage referrals, facilitate telehealth services, communicate with healthcare providers, and maintain accurate EMR documentation. My previous healthcare administration experience includes insurance verification, benefits eligibility, and patient registration.

Additionally, my experience as a 911 Emergency Dispatcher strengthened my skills in crisis communication, de-escalation, active listening, high-volume call management, and critical thinking. I understand the importance of providing compassionate, nonjudgmental support to individuals and families experiencing difficult circumstances.

My qualifications include:

- Patient intake, screening, and referral coordination
- Insurance verification and benefits eligibility
- High-volume inbound and outbound calls
- Appointment scheduling and patient follow-up
- Telehealth and healthcare navigation
- Crisis communication and de-escalation
- EMR documentation and HIPAA compliance
- Independent caseload management and problem-solving

I am passionate about helping individuals and families overcome barriers to healthcare. I welcome the opportunity to apply my transferable skills to behavioral health admissions, substance use treatment, and coordination of Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP) and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP).

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my clinical background, administrative experience, and commitment to compassionate patient support can contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Jennifer M. Hicks, LPN

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With more than 15 years of experience in social services, case management, and client advocacy, I bring a strong background in working with children, adolescents, and families experiencing challenging circumstances. Throughout my career, I have developed a passion for helping individuals access the support and resources they need, particularly during some of the most difficult periods of their lives.

As a Family Specialist with Community Providers for Adolescent Social Services, I worked closely with children, adolescents, and their families, serving as a liaison between clients, social workers, schools, legal advocates, and community providers. My responsibilities included assessing family needs, coordinating services, identifying appropriate resources, and maintaining consistent communication with everyone involved in supporting each family’s well-being. This experience taught me the importance of approaching sensitive situations with compassion, patience, and professionalism while ensuring families felt heard and supported.

A significant part of my experience involved conducting client assessments, gathering and reviewing supporting documentation, coordinating referrals, and following up to ensure individuals received the services they needed. I managed caseloads of 8 to 15 families simultaneously, often meeting with families multiple times per week while maintaining detailed records of phone calls, meetings, correspondence, and case progress. I understand the importance of timely follow-up, accurate documentation, confidentiality, and maintaining an organized caseload to ensure that no client falls through the cracks.

In my subsequent roles in case management and financial coaching, I continued developing my ability to communicate with individuals and families, identify barriers, navigate complex service systems, and connect clients with appropriate resources. I also gained experience conducting phone-based and virtual appointments, managing sensitive client information, and maintaining accurate records in database systems. These skills translate well to coordinating admissions, communicating with prospective clients and families, and helping them navigate the next steps toward receiving care.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to make a meaningful difference at the very beginning of someone’s treatment journey. I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be overwhelming for individuals and their families. I believe my background, empathy, persistence, and ability to build trusting relationships would allow me to provide the reassurance and guidance callers need during that process.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience and commitment to helping others to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills can contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Phillip Perez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to combine my professional experience in coordination and customer service with something I genuinely care about: helping individuals and families find the support and resources they need during some of the most difficult periods of their lives.

My interest in this field is also personal. Through my own life experiences, I understand how overwhelming it can be to navigate mental health challenges, search for appropriate treatment, locate community resources, and figure out where to turn when you don’t know what options are available. I know firsthand how much of a difference it can make when someone takes the time to listen, treats you with compassion rather than judgment, and helps you navigate the next steps. I would love the opportunity to be that person for families who may be feeling overwhelmed, scared, or unsure of where to begin.

Professionally, I bring a diverse background in customer service, independent operations, event coordination, and administrative responsibilities. In previous positions, I have been responsible for coordinating activities, communicating with a wide range of individuals, managing schedules and logistics, resolving problems, maintaining organization, and handling multiple responsibilities independently. I have also worked in roles requiring patience, adaptability, strong communication skills, and the ability to remain composed when situations become challenging.

I believe one of my greatest strengths is my ability to understand people without making assumptions about their circumstances. I recognize that every individual and family has a different story, and I would approach every interaction with empathy, patience, professionalism, and respect. I am also comfortable learning new systems, following established procedures, and taking initiative when something needs to be done.

I am looking for a long-term career where I can grow professionally while doing work that has a meaningful impact on other people’s lives. The opportunity to help adolescents and their families take the first steps toward receiving mental health and substance use treatment is something I would take seriously and approach with genuine compassion.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my professional background, personal perspective, and dedication to helping others could make me a valuable addition to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team.

Sincerely,
Amber

work_history.title: Medical Assistant
work_history.summary: During my position here I worked as a Medical Assistant. I would room patients get there chief complaint as to why they were there for the visit, write down any refills of medications that they needed, take their vitals (temperature, blood pressure, pulse, heart rate, and oxygen saturation), have them fill out any paperwork needed before the provider or doctor got into the room, and wrote down any questions or concerns that they had, I would chart prep for the next day before leaving (print off medication list, MICR, lab report/radiology report if needed, pre-fill out any paperwork that was pertaining to that visit, and/or look up any information needed for the visit), I would check emails to make sure nothing needed attention throughout the day, check messages throughout the day to see if anything needed to be ordered or done, I gave immunizations (influenza, Covid, pneumonia, TDap, HPV, ect.), answer phone calls as needed throughout the day, refill medications or "propose" them to the provider or doctor if needed throughout the day, stock patient rooms, collect urine samples, collect blood for A1C tests, run urine dipsticks, pregnancy tests, swabbed for flu/covid/strep/rsv, scheduled patients if they needed to be, do EKG's if needed, call any other doctors office/ especially office/pharmacy if the provider or doctor needed me to go get more information, triage phone calls if they were having chest pains/stroke symptoms/other serious or emergent issues to see if they needed to go to the emergency room or if we can see them in the office. I also cleaned the rooms every night before leaving. I cleaned and wiped down/sanitized the beds, tables, and blood pressure utensils after every patient. I would also do/help with any other work needed either by coworkers or my boss whether it be calling patients back, calling patients with test results, doing paperwork, or anything else that I knew how to do. I would call on referrals to see where the status is for patients to help them get the best care they need if things are taking longer than expected as well. I also would help answer phone calls, document messages, and transfer calls where they were needed to go. I would also do some investigating if a patient called with issues and we couldn't find where or what they were looking for. I transcribed or entered lab results as well into the patient's chart. I would take phone calls and try to help patient's resolve any issues they were having and try to calm them down if they were upset so we could figure out what was going on. Lastly, I would do some stocking and take inventory of everything we had to see if anything needed to be ordered.

work_history.title: Title Unknown
work_history.summary: I was in the Patient Access Service Department where I worked third shift, 7pm-7am, in the Emergency Department checking in the patients when they came in. I would get their date of birth, name, what they were there for, their insurance, driver's license, get their signature on the consent form, then print off labels for the nurses, and put the reason why the patient was here to be seen for on top of the label sheet. Then once the ER doctor has gone and saw them in whatever room they were in I would go into the room and verify that the patient's address, phone number, emergency contact, and family doctor is all correct in our system. Also, later on in the night I would run our billing reports, download the billing reports as well, and do the referrals and renames that needed to be done. Inventory Help

work_history.title: Title Unknown
work_history.summary: I oversaw cleaning up their inventory and help solve any of the "mysteries" that may have appeared. I made sure that their inventory matches what is in their AX software system, so they can reference the items. I also took pictures of the parts in their inventor and upload them into the AX software for all of the workers can use them as a reference if they need to. I communicated with all of the workers in the shop, so we can try and come up with a situation if there are any problem that occur.

work_history.title: Customer Service

work_history.title: Cashier/Customer Service
work_history.summary: I worked at the customer service desk checking people out when they were done shopping. I would also greet them as they came into the store as well. When I was not busy I would be cleaning up the front of the store near the customer service desk and the front of the apparel section. I would also answer the phones for the customers who had called and had a question or questions about something, I would transfer them to correct department they needed. I also knew how to do returns for the customers who had bought something that had either not worked or they did not like it like they thought they would. I would organize the returns I had behind the desk into each department category so at the end of the night when they got taken to the back room so they can be taken care of the next day. Hostess Applebee's Coldwater, MI June 2015 to September 2015 I was a host, so I greeted people as they came in the door and would sit them in either a booth or table, which ever one they preferred, and gave them their menu's and silverware and would tell them who their server was for the afternoon/ evening. I also had the job of busting of the tables when the customers left which is where I basically clean it all off and wipe down the table. I would also run food out to tables if it was crazy busy to help the servers out a little bit. One last thing I had done was learn how people can really read you as a person so if you are in a bad mood and showing it then the customers will see that so therefore, I had learned to always put a smile on my face no matter what was going on and no matter how bad by day was going.

work_history.title: Volunteer

Whether it is doing one-on-one help with students to help them understand the subject or to catch up on their homework or helping then stay focused.
