Taran Pietosi West Mifflin, PA 15122 · 412-530-8058· Taran.pietosi@gmail.com · linkedin.com/in/taran-pietosi 


Dear Hiring Team,
People don't call a treatment program on a good day. That first conversation has to slow things down, get the facts that matter, and leave the caller with a clear next step. I'm applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role because that's the work I already do on the disaster side, and I want to do it full-time helping people get into care.
Since December 2024 I've volunteered as a Duty Officer with the American Red Cross. When a home fire or other disaster displaces a family, the Duty Officer is often the first person the family or the fire department reaches. I take the call, figure out what the family needs, decide what response fits, and coordinate until they're connected to help. 
It's intake under pressure: listening past the panic, asking the right questions in the right order, and following through so nobody falls through the cracks.
My current role as a Regional Event Admin in RC Care is the record-keeping side of that same work. I create and correct disaster event records, keep client data accurate and confidential, and build the Excel reports regional leadership uses to track responder availability and training gaps. I understand that a record is only useful if it's right, and I pick up new case-management systems quickly. Both roles are largely self-directed and done remotely by phone and computer, so I'm used to managing my own workload without daily direction.
I also have direct experience providing peer support to people in addiction recovery, and I'm currently studying trauma psychology. I hold Naloxone Administration, First Aid, and Bloodborne Pathogens certifications. Earlier, I worked in a call center at DialAmerica, where I learned to stay professional and productive across a steady volume of calls.
I haven't held a formal admissions title at a treatment facility. What I bring is the core of the job: first-contact screening of people in crisis, a calm and caring phone presence, accurate and confidential records, and the follow-through to keep working a case until every caller has a next step. I'd welcome the chance to talk about how that experience fits your team.
Sincerely,
Taran Pietosi

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, professional experience in behavioural health and mental health settings, and fluency in both English and Spanish, I believe I could bring a strong combination of clinical understanding, communication skills, and compassion to your team.

My background includes working as a Registered Behavior Technician, supporting children and adolescents with autism and other developmental needs. In this role, I worked closely with families and clinical teams, followed individualised treatment plans, documented progress, maintained accurate records, and communicated regularly with parents and supervisors. This experience taught me the importance of building trust, being patient, and recognising that every family has different needs.

I have also worked as a Mental Health Assistant within a hospital setting, where I gained experience supporting individuals experiencing mental health difficulties, communicating with patients and multidisciplinary teams, and understanding the importance of confidentiality, accurate documentation, and compassionate care. My psychology education has further strengthened my understanding of mental health, behavioural challenges, and the importance of connecting individuals with appropriate support.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is being able to make a difference at the very first point of contact. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an incredibly difficult step, both for individuals and their families. I would approach every conversation with empathy, professionalism, and the ability to explain information clearly without making people feel overwhelmed or judged.

As a bilingual English and Spanish speaker, I would also be comfortable supporting Spanish-speaking families and individuals who may otherwise find navigating the treatment process more difficult.

I am organised, comfortable managing multiple responsibilities, and take pride in following through on tasks and maintaining accurate documentation. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my behavioural health experience and genuine interest in helping people access treatment to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would love the opportunity to discuss how my experience and background could contribute to your admissions team.

Kind regards,
Melanie Fernandez

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I am drawn to the opportunity to be part of an organization that helps individuals and families navigate some of life's most difficult circumstances and connect with the care and support they need. I believe that compassion, patience, and effective communication can make an extraordinary difference in someone's willingness to take that first step toward healing.

Throughout my professional career, I have developed extensive experience in management, customer relations, administrative operations, and working with individuals from diverse backgrounds. My management experience has strengthened my ability to listen carefully, assess individual needs, navigate challenging conversations, resolve concerns, and guide people through unfamiliar processes. I understand the importance of remaining calm and professional under pressure while ensuring that every person feels heard, respected, and supported.

My background also includes working in highly detail-oriented and safety-sensitive environments where accurate documentation, confidentiality, organization, and adherence to established procedures are essential. I am comfortable managing multiple priorities, learning new software systems, maintaining records, and following through on responsibilities without needing constant supervision. I am technologically proficient, adaptable, and confident communicating professionally over the phone and through written correspondence.

In addition to my professional experience, I hold four associate degrees, technical certifications, and CPR/BLS certification. I am also a California-licensed real estate professional, an experience that has further strengthened my ability to understand individual circumstances, explain complicated processes, handle sensitive information, and guide people through important decisions. Across my various professional roles, I have learned that building trust begins with listening, communicating clearly, and treating every individual with dignity.

What particularly appeals to me about this position is the opportunity to make a meaningful difference before someone even begins treatment. I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use support can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience, not only for the individual but also for their loved ones. I would approach every interaction with empathy, professionalism, discretion, and a genuine commitment to helping callers understand their options and take the next step toward receiving care.

I am eager to continue developing my knowledge of healthcare admissions, insurance verification, and electronic medical record systems while bringing my existing organizational, communication, and leadership skills to your team. I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to an organization whose work has such a meaningful impact on individuals and families.

I also have professional recommendation letters and references available upon request and would be pleased to provide them during the hiring process.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my professional background, education, and commitment to helping others could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Suzanne Ornelas-Pelaez

candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over four years of combined experience in healthcare, behavioral health, and hospital administration, I have developed a strong foundation in patient-centered care, communication, clinical documentation, and administrative support.

My experience at The Vines Hospital has allowed me to develop a well-rounded understanding of hospital operations through both clinical and administrative responsibilities. As a Mental Health Technician, I work directly with patients experiencing mental health challenges, assist with maintaining a safe therapeutic environment, observe and document patient behaviors, and collaborate with nursing staff and interdisciplinary teams.

Additionally, I have several months of experience working as a Receptionist at The Vines Hospital. This experience strengthened my administrative and customer service skills while providing additional exposure to the front-end operations of a healthcare facility. Having experience on both the clinical and administrative sides of behavioral healthcare has given me a broader understanding of the importance of effective communication, organization, professionalism, and creating positive first impressions for patients and families.

I have also received training in verbal de-escalation, including techniques focused on empathy, communication, and managing power struggles. These skills are particularly valuable when interacting with individuals and families who may be experiencing emotional distress, uncertainty, or difficulty navigating the treatment process. I understand that seeking mental health or substance use treatment can be overwhelming, and I believe every individual deserves to be treated with compassion, dignity, and respect.

My previous experience as a Patient Care Technician and Nurse Extern with HCA Healthcare further strengthened my clinical knowledge, documentation skills, and ability to work effectively in fast-paced healthcare environments. I gained experience assisting with patient care, supporting nursing staff, monitoring patient needs, and maintaining professional communication while prioritizing patient safety.

I bring strong organizational skills, attention to detail, adaptability, and an understanding of the importance of confidentiality and accurate information. I recognize that the admissions process is often a family’s first interaction with a treatment program, and I would take pride in making that experience welcoming, informative, and supportive.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my behavioral health experience, administrative background, and passion for helping individuals access appropriate treatment. I am comfortable communicating with patients and families, collaborating with healthcare professionals, and adapting to changing priorities.

I believe my combination of clinical, administrative, and behavioral health experience would make me a valuable addition to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to the admissions process and help ensure adolescents and their families receive the guidance, professionalism, and support they deserve when seeking treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and qualifications align with the needs of your organization.

Sincerely,

Davionia Day

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, experience in behavioral health case management, and fluency in English and Spanish, I would bring compassionate communication, strong organizational skills, and a commitment to helping families access care.

As a Targeted Case Manager with Advanced Health Community Services since 2022, I support children, adolescents, and adults experiencing mental health challenges and complex barriers to treatment. My responsibilities include identifying service needs, coordinating referrals, communicating with providers, assisting with appointments, and following up with families to support continuity of care. This work requires accurate documentation, attention to confidentiality, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while remaining responsive to each family’s needs.

I have experience supporting adolescents and caregivers navigating depression, anxiety, trauma, behavioral challenges, and psychiatric hospitalizations. I understand how overwhelming seeking treatment can feel, and I approach families with patience, empathy, and clear explanations. My bilingual skills also allow me to communicate directly with Spanish-speaking families and help reduce language barriers.

I am eager to bring these transferable skills to admissions, helping families understand next steps, coordinating with clinical teams, and supporting a timely transition into appropriate treatment. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your team and help adolescents and their families feel supported from their first contact.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my experience and dedication to accessible behavioral health care align with this position.

Sincerely,
Ledy Martinez

Manuel Garcia, MA, LADC, CAC, ICADC

November 18, 2026

Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Re: Program Director, Virtual Intensive Outpatient Program

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to apply for the Program Director, Virtual IOP position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over a decade of progressive leadership experience at Hazelden Betty Ford and Caron Treatment Centers, I have built, expanded, and led behavioral health programs that combine clinical excellence with sustainable business performance. What particularly attracts me to this opportunity is the chance to bring together two areas where I have demonstrated significant success: developing accessible virtual treatment services and leading programs through strategic growth.

At Hazelden Betty Ford, I spearheaded the development and implementation of English and Spanish virtual behavioral health services in just two weeks during the COVID-19 pandemic. This required rapidly establishing clinical workflows, adapting treatment delivery to a virtual environment, supporting multidisciplinary teams, and maintaining continuity of care without compromising clinical quality. Beyond this initiative, I helped standardize intensive outpatient programming and curriculum across multiple markets, including Minnesota, New York, Chicago, and California. These experiences strengthened my ability to scale accessible treatment models while maintaining operational consistency and clinical integrity.

Currently, as Senior Clinical Director for Caron Treatment Centers in Florida, I provide strategic and operational leadership across a comprehensive continuum of behavioral healthcare services. My responsibilities encompass clinical operations, financial performance, program development, staff leadership, regulatory compliance, and quality improvement. I have helped expand treatment capacity from startup operations to approximately 75 beds within months, supported programs serving more than 500 patients annually, and implemented systems to strengthen documentation quality, operational accountability, and the patient experience.

What distinguishes my leadership approach is the belief that exceptional clinical care and strong business performance are mutually reinforcing. Sustainable census growth depends on meaningful referral relationships, reliable operational systems, measurable outcomes, and an experience that earns the trust of patients, families, and community partners. I lead with a commitment to high standards, thoughtful innovation, and personalized service, ensuring that operational decisions ultimately strengthen the quality and accessibility of care.

Adolescent Wellness Academy’s family-centered approach and commitment to expanding access to treatment for adolescents strongly resonate with me. I would welcome the opportunity to apply my experience in virtual care development, multidisciplinary leadership, financial oversight, and program growth to build a high-performing Virtual IOP that creates meaningful outcomes for young people and their families throughout Florida.

Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and leadership philosophy can contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s continued growth and mission.

Sincerely,

Manuel Garcia, MA, LADC, CAC, ICADC

Dear AWA Hiring Team,

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I'm excited to apply for the Operations Manager position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and the opportunity to help establish your first North Carolina clinic. With over 15 years of experience in administrative operations, team leadership, healthcare coordination, and program management, I bring a strong foundation in building efficient, supportive, and accountable work environments.

Most recently, as Administrative Coordinator at Pyramid Healthcare, I supported daily operations at a secure inpatient detoxification and residential treatment facility serving approximately 100 patients. My responsibilities included admissions and discharge coordination, program scheduling, confidential documentation, facility management, vendor relations, and collaboration with clinical leadership. Through proactive process improvements, I reduced monthly client supply costs by approximately 40% without compromising quality.

My previous leadership positions as a Department Head and Office Manager strengthened my skills in employee supervision, training, financial oversight, and operational efficiency. Additionally, my experience as a YMCA youth soccer coach and Girl Scout troop leader reflects my genuine passion for mentoring, encouraging, and supporting young people.

The opportunity to combine my behavioral healthcare experience, leadership abilities, and enthusiasm for youth development while helping build a program from the ground up is particularly exciting.

I currently reside in Vanceboro, NC, and am actively seeking to relocate to the Mooresville area. Upon receiving a formal offer of employment, I am prepared to relocate promptly and coordinate a start date that aligns with the clinic's opening.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my initiative, compassion, and solutions-oriented leadership style to AWA's founding North Carolina team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Amanda Robinson

I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Program Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Psychology graduate, I have been looking for an opportunity to work in a mental health setting where I can contribute to something meaningful while continuing to develop professionally. I enjoy remote work and the organization and communication that come with it, but what matters most to me is knowing that my work is helping people.

My interest in this field has grown even stronger since beginning my volunteer experience with the Alachua Crisis Center. It has reminded me how important it is to have people who are willing to listen, offer support, and help others through difficult moments. It has also made me realize how much I want my everyday work to be connected to making a difference in someone's life.

I previously worked at Nicaragua Recovery, a residential recovery program, where I supported patients through daily check-ins, activities, and recovery programming. I facilitated daily One Day at a Time reflection groups and translated the discussions into English for patients who did not speak Spanish so they could participate fully. I also interpreted conversations between patients and their outside caregivers, helping make communication easier and ensuring patients could better understand and express themselves. Later, I worked remotely as an Outreach Coordinator for the same program, contacting prospective patients, explaining the program, answering questions, and communicating with clinics and therapists about potential referrals.

In my current remote administrative position, I manage correspondence, organize information, communicate with customers, and coordinate with different departments. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to stay organized, communicate clearly, and manage tasks independently. I would be excited to bring these skills into a mental health setting where the administrative work directly supports patients, families, and clinical teams.

As a native English and Spanish speaker with a degree in Psychology, I would value the opportunity to contribute to AWA's work with adolescents and their families. I am dependable, eager to learn, and genuinely motivated to build a career in a field where I can help others.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to speak with you about how my background and motivation could contribute to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to connect and discuss how my experience and values align with your organization.

Warm regards,
Christina Samuda

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I hold a degree in Psychology and Human Development and Family Sciences and have hands-on experience working with adolescents and adults in behavioral health and residential treatment settings. In both psychiatric rehabilitation and substance use treatment facilities, I facilitated visual arts, stretching and movement, and psychosocial rehabilitation groups. Combined with my professional background in dance and creative expression, I bring a skill set that closely aligns with this position.

**Group Facilitation & Behavioral Health Experience**

My experience in residential behavioral health has involved facilitating groups designed to promote emotional well-being, social development, and personal growth. My psychosocial rehabilitation groups focused on strengthening everyday life skills, improving social functioning, developing healthy coping strategies, and increasing independence. Through structured activities, group discussions, and interactive exercises, I encouraged participants to practice communication, problem-solving, self-awareness, and positive interpersonal skills.

I also bring experience working with adolescents in youth development and residential settings. These experiences have strengthened my ability to build rapport, adapt activities to different developmental needs, manage group dynamics, and create supportive environments where young people feel comfortable participating.

**Dance & Creative Expression**

In addition to my behavioral health experience, I have a longstanding background in dance and movement. I studied classical dance at Miami Arts, served as a choreographer with Florida State University's Belly Dance Troupe, and have professional dance and performance experience.

I enjoy using movement and creative expression to encourage confidence, body awareness, self-expression, and personal growth. I would love to incorporate these interests into engaging group activities that help adolescents explore new ways to connect with themselves and others.

I am particularly drawn to AWA's approach to combining mental health support with creative and experiential programming. The opportunity to bring together my experience in group facilitation, behavioral health, adolescent development, and the arts is especially meaningful to me.

Thank you for your consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience could contribute to your programming and the adolescents you serve.

Sincerely,  
Athena V. Sullivan

Dear Hiring Team,

I'm excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background in Studio Art and Psychology, as well as experience in Special Education and Applied Behavior Analysis, I have always been drawn to the ways creativity can help us connect, express ourselves, and discover more about who we are. I would love the opportunity to bring this perspective into a setting that supports adolescents through their mental health journeys.

In my current role as a SpEd Art Teacher, I work with students with diverse learning needs, developing creative activities to encourage their exploration and independence. My approach to art is centered on the process rather than the final product; I believe the arts should be an opportunity to experiment, take risks, make mistakes, and express yourself without the pressure of getting something "right." My previous experience as an ABA Teacher has also taught me the importance of meeting individuals where they are and creating supportive environments where everyone feels welcome to participate.

My creative background extends beyond visual art to include writing, music, and theatre. These experiences have deepened my appreciation for the many ways people communicate and express themselves, and I'm drawn to opportunities that allow others to explore those possibilities.

My connection to art is also personal. Throughout my own experiences, creativity has been a meaningful way to process and make sense of my emotions. I've come to appreciate the value of having the space to process without judgement or expectations. This is an environment I hope to foster for others; one where individuals feel safe to explore their emotions, connect with each other, and perhaps even learn something new about themselves along the way.

I would be grateful for the chance to contribute my creativity and enthusiasm for the therapeutic arts to the AWA community. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Best,
Charity Ortiz, BA, RBT
